summary: No must-fix. All five files satisfy the general rules (true peak -15.3 to -5.0 dBFS, DC below 1e-6, onset under 1 ms, last 10 ms below -95 dBFS, no click outside the intended attacks, shield bass equal in both channels, loudness within 0.1 dB across the thrusters and 1.2 dB across the shields). Five flags, no pass. The shared weak spots: the low end of thruster_c and the hum of shield_b are narrow, steady lines (one 88 Hz line holds 88 % of thruster_c by Welch, five ruler-straight partials in shield_b), and the listening models name something else for most files. I measured with my own numpy script and did not open the agent's module or report file; the comparison uses the summary quoted in the brief. Nothing was heard by a person.

Max step / p99.9 = 1.6. Spectrogram: a broadband jet from 0 to 0.2 s, strongest around 1 to 2 kHz, with haze up to 20 kHz, a hard cut at about 0.2 s, then a low body at 80 to 200 Hz sliding down to 70 Hz by 0.35 s; no ruler-straight line, no repeated pings. CLAP: 'a short sharp burst of compressed gas from a nozzle' 0.157, but the negative with the same meaning (0.171) is on top; taut foil 0.117 is third, above 'a spacecraft manoeuvring thruster firing a short puff' (-0.066). Qwen2-Audio: 'the onomatopoeia sound of a squeak'.
sounds.described: Gas jet: click, 150-250 ms hiss, closing click, hull thump 70-160 Hz. Targets 55 / 15 / 10-25 % are met.
problems: All numeric targets are met, but the jet is a block, not a swell and a fall. In 5 ms steps the high band is at 0 dB from 0 to 15 ms and then stays between -3 and -11 dB until about 175 ms, then falls 30 dB in 40 ms. There is no swell, only flutter of about plus/minus 5 dB. The brief asked for fast swell, slightly slower fall, alive and not a flat block.

Between the click (1 ms RMS -23 dB at 0 ms) and the jet (about -25 to -34 dB from 6 ms) the level falls to -53 dB for 3 to 4 ms, 20 to 30 dB below the jet. That can be heard as two events (a tick, then a hiss). The agent's note says 2 ms and 30 dB; I measure 3 to 4 ms.

19.9 % of the energy is above 8 kHz and the spectrogram shows haze to 20 kHz. This is the thin, hissy side that the earlier words 'toy' and 'taut foil' describe; CLAP puts foil third and Qwen answers 'squeak' (a weak model, but the answer is a high thin sound, not gas).
A bleed hiss at -67 dB runs from 0.27 s to the end; harmless at that level.

Spectrogram: no vertical attack line is visible at this time resolution (the crack sits inside the first column); a low body at 90 to 250 Hz sliding down to 55 Hz by 0.2 s, a separate patch of noise at 4 to 20 kHz fading by 0.2 s, and a clean dark gap from 500 Hz to 3 kHz. CLAP: taut plastic foil 0.103 is on top, above the file's own best positive (0.070) and above the energy shield text (0.087); compressed gas 0.054, plastic container -0.091. sounds.described: Cinema punch: bright crack, chesty 100-300 Hz punch dropping in pitch, short airy tail. Targets (attack centre at or above 2 kHz, 40-60 % below 500 Hz, at least 25 % above 1 kHz) are met.
problems: CLAP ranks 'someone tapping on a taut plastic foil' first. The spectrum explains it: 38 % of the energy is noise at 4 to 20 kHz and almost nothing sits between 500 Hz and 3 kHz (1.1 + 2.9 + 6.0 % in three octaves). A hollow between a low punch and air is what a foil or a cheap drum machine sounds like. Qwen's 'kick drum' is the intended game-punch reading.

The attack centre of 2.8 kHz holds only with a rectangular window; with a Hann window it reads 0.64 kHz (the agent states this). Over the first 7 ms the crack is 89 % above 1 kHz, over 10 ms 67 %, so the character is in the data, but the crack is weak against a body that carries 52 % of the file.
Peak step 3.7 times p99.9 at sample 1 of the file: a hard first-sample jump. It is the attack by design, but it is a real discontinuity at t=0 and may tick on a player that applies no fade-in.

First 7 ms 96.5 % above 1 kHz, first 10 ms 86.2 %, first 30 ms 41.3 %; the agent's 41.3 % is the 30 ms window, so the target 'at least 50 % of the attack above 1 kHz' is met if the attack is the 5-10 ms clack and missed if it is 30 ms. CLAP: own best 'a solenoid valve clacking with a tight low thump' 0.142 is on top, clearly the best; the energy shield text 0.119 is second; plastic container 0.028; foil 0.021. Qwen2-Audio: 'a door tapping lightly with each step'.
sounds.described: Solenoid clack 2-5 kHz and a tight 60-140 Hz thump, no hiss. At least 60 % below 250 Hz (61.3, narrow) and at most 10 % above 1 kHz after 15 ms (0.8) are met; for the attack share see problems.
problems: One spectral line carries 88 % of the file by Welch, 54 % by whole-file FFT: a sine blip at about 88 Hz falling to 56 Hz. On laptop speakers or small headphones that cannot reproduce 60 to 100 Hz, what remains is the 5 ms clack, a tick. Qwen answers 'door tapping', a knocking reading, although CLAP's plastic-container score is low (0.028, rank 4 of 10).
Attack-share target: 96.5 % (7 ms) and 86 % (10 ms) above 1 kHz pass, 41.3 % over 30 ms fails. The target needs a stated window; the clack character is there, so this alone is not a must-fix.
Below 250 Hz is 61.3 % against a floor of 60 %: a hair of margin. The clack is only 37.9 % of the file and the thump 61 %; the sound leans dull and low more than crisp.
Largest step 3.3 times p99.9 at the start: the intended clack, no click mid-file.

sounds.described: Keep crackle and hiss of the medium shield hit; add a 45-90 Hz throb that swells in 30 ms, beats at 6-12 Hz, decays over at least 0.9 s; add a 250 Hz-2 kHz growl. Targets low band within 12 dB for 0.4 s, 30 %, 15 %, 15 %, equal bass in both channels: all met.
problems: Beat rate: my estimate of the strongest 40-125 Hz envelope component is 12.9 Hz, above the asked 6-12 Hz (the agent reports the same 12.9). The estimator is rough, but the numbers agree, so it is a small miss.

53 Hz holds 30 to 35 % of the energy in a single peak. By ear that is a standing hum that sits almost flat for 1.2 s (the low block in the spectrogram barely decays) more than a decaying throb. The brief gave no peak limit for A; shield B has one (15 %).

Isolated crackle bursts at 0.55 s and 0.98 s (the later one reaches 12 kHz while everything else above 2 kHz is below -60 dB) stand out as separate ticks long after the crackle has died; Qwen's 'whip cracking' answer fits those.
True peak -5.0 dBFS is the loudest of the five and 2.1 dB above shield B; the owner asked whether the library might be too loud and overdriven. Rule limit is -1, so this is only a note.

sounds.described: Cinema: a deep whoomp 120 to 40 Hz leads, soft sizzle (10-25 % above 2 kHz, at most 5 % above 8 kHz), field hum of three to five inharmonic beating partials 180-700 Hz. At least 40 % below 250 Hz (45.2), low band maximum within 60 ms (20 ms), at least 15 % at 250 Hz-2 kHz (30.6), 24.2 % above 2 kHz, 0.1 % above 8 kHz: all met.
problems: The hum is five straight lines that hold for 1.2 s with no drift. That reads as a synthesiser pad or a guitar (Qwen says 'guitar with distortion'), not as a living field. CLAP's own positives are weak (0.105 and -0.014).

Only 2.1 % of the file is below 60 Hz and the low band is inside 12 dB for only 140 ms (-33 dB at 0.4 s). The deep whoomp is short and mostly 60 to 250 Hz (43 %); the owner asked that energetic sounds always have a bass throb. Shield A has it; B has a kick that is gone before the hum has started.

Peak share 15.8 % at 270 Hz (whole-file, three bins either side) is above the 15 % limit; 13.0 % by Welch and 5.2 % in the agent's whole-file number. The brief does not say which window counts, so this is borderline.
Above 2 kHz is 24.2 % against a ceiling of 25 %, and 250-500 Hz holds 20.1 % (the hum): small margins on several numbers.

contrast: THRUSTERS (same loudness: -33.96, -33.96, -34.04 LUFS, so no family loudness problem). They are clearly different answers. A: 74.5 % above 1 kHz, 44.2 % above 4 kHz, 17 % below 250 Hz, jet 200 ms long (high band within 12 dB for 200 ms), low band max at 220 ms (the thump comes last), centroid 4774 Hz, true peak -15.3. B: 52 % below 500 Hz, 37.7 % above 4 kHz, a hole of 1.1 + 2.9 + 6.0 % from 500 Hz to 4 kHz, low band max at 20 ms and within 12 dB for 100 ms (the thump comes first), high band 80 ms, centroid 3866 Hz, true peak -9.0. C: 61.3 % below 250 Hz, 11.5 % above 4 kHz, 0.8 % above 1 kHz after 15 ms, 88 % in one 88 Hz line, everything inside 60 ms, centroid 1445 Hz, true peak -9.3. B and C both start with a first-sample knock and a thump whose largest whole-file peak sits at 84 to 86 Hz, but B has a 250 ms noise tail with 38 % above 4 kHz and a 250-500 Hz body that C lacks (19.4 % against 0.4 %), so they are not near-copies. SHIELDS (-23.69 and -24.88 LUFS, 1.2 dB apart). A: low band within 12 dB for 700 ms contiguous, 16 % below 60 Hz, 31.5 % at 60-125 Hz, crackle to 0.55 s plus a stray burst at 0.98 s, 30 % in the 53 Hz peak, true peak -5.0, centroid 1402 Hz, 5.0 % above 8 kHz. B: low band within 12 dB for 140 ms, 2 % below 60 Hz, whoomp at 60-250 Hz (43 %), sustained five-line hum at 180-620 Hz (250-500 Hz holds 20 %), 24 % above 2 kHz but only 0.1 % above 8 kHz, true peak -7.2, centroid 1052 Hz. A is a long bass throb with crackle, B a short whoomp with a pad; clearly different. EARLIER WORDS. 'Plastic container' (dull knock): thruster_c is the only candidate by its numbers (a tight 88 Hz blip with a small click; Qwen says 'door tapping'), but CLAP puts the plastic container at 0.028, rank 4 of 10, far below its own positive 0.142, so a small risk, not a certain return. 'Under water': no file is muffled by the numbers (centroids 1.0 to 4.8 kHz, 11 to 61 % above 2 kHz; CLAP 'a sound heard under water' between -0.055 and +0.064, rank 6 to 9 of 10). 'Taut foil': thruster_b (CLAP rank 1, 0.103; a hollow from 500 Hz to 3 kHz plus 38 % air above 4 kHz) and thruster_a (rank 3, 0.117; 19.9 % above 8 kHz, flat jet) carry the risk; shield_a scores 0.169 for foil but below its own positives, shield_b 0.069.
notVerified: Nothing was heard by a person or by me: all verdicts come from instruments and two models.
Qwen2-Audio and CLAP are weak judges of 0.35 to 1.6 s synthetic clips. Qwen's answers ('squeak', 'whip and a dog', 'guitar') are hints, not measurements; CLAP only orders the descriptions.

The beat rate in shield_a is a crude estimate (5 ms RMS envelope of a 4th-order 40-125 Hz band-pass, spectrum of the envelope between 3 and 30 Hz); the 12.9 Hz may be partly an artefact of the band-pass.

The peak-share numbers depend on the window: I give whole-file Hann with 3 bins either side and 8192-sample Welch with the same 3 bins. The brief does not fix a window, so the shield_b limit of 15 % is borderline either way.
My LUFS (levels.lufs on the stereo file) differs from the -28.3 the build JSON states for both shields by 4.6 dB; I did not find out why. Only the differences inside a family were judged.
The judgement 'jet flat, not alive' for thruster_a rests on a 5 ms RMS envelope of the band above 1.5 kHz, not on a listening test.

I did not read pilot-energy-report.json or cat_pilot_energy.py; the comparison uses the agent's summary quoted in the brief. I did not check the other pilot_* files (gear, hull) and did not run the test suite.
No file in the repository was changed except this report; my measuring scripts are in my scratch directory.
